domain.decoder: the key denominator: 6 factors R_j, each an integer coefficient list coeffs (leading coefficient first) with an integer multiplicity m_j (3, 3, 2, 2, 1, 2); the key numerator: 7 factors S_i, each an integer coefficient list coeffs with a rational exponent q_rational = q_i > 0; the file is the construction Épi's result.json names, whose artifact_sha256 equals the pin

g.named: Doche's limit-point bound B = ( log M(Q∘T) + ∫_0^1 max(0, Σ_i q_i log|S_i∘T(e^{2πit})| − Σ_j m_j log|R_j∘T(e^{2πit})|) dt ) / D with T(z) = z(1 − z), Q = Π_j R_j^{m_j}, D = Σ_j m_j deg R_j and M the Mahler measure, enclosed by sound arithmetic once the hypotheses of Doche's theorem hold exactly: integer factors with the denominators monic up to sign, Σ_i q_i deg S_i < D, gcd(S_i, R_j) = 1 for q_i > 0, and every root of every composed factor isolated

reference: the bar is the registry's printed 0.2535744749068227 taken exactly (sixteen decimals; the number Épi's README and result.json print as the displayed upper bound, "rounded outward"); the quantity is the construction's limit-point bound B, enclosed by the record at [0.2535689301873338, 0.25356893042349005] (B.js; B.py agrees), whose upper end is below the bar by 5.5e-6 — the printed bound is weaker than the construction gives, on the safe side, and the row's comment quotes [Pin26]'s re-evaluation 0.25356893…, which the record's enclosure contains; the relation is <= as the upper-bounds table and the record's claim string read it (no strict print for this row)
hypotheses: Doche's theorem [Doc01b] (the limit-point argument: U^n − W^n over the primes, Jensen's formula, coprimality), also proved in the claimant [Pin26]'s README: for integer factors with the stated hypotheses, infinitely many distinct algebraic numbers have h_Z <= B, so C_82 <= B (read, not re-derived)
the definition on the 82a page: C_82 is the supremum of the H for which {α : h_Z(α) <= H} is finite, h_Z(α) = h(α) + h(1 − α) (read)
the integrand is symmetric under t → 1 − t (real coefficients), so the integral over [0, 1/2] doubled is the integral over [0, 1] (read; the record's limit)
falsifier: the enclosure of B computed from the pinned factors has its lower end above 2535744749068227/10000000000000000 (REFUTED), or straddles it (REFUSED)
